targets.title: Deep Interactions With MRP: Election Turnout and Voting Patterns Among Small Electoral Subgroups
targets.evidence_quote: In Ghitza and Gelman (2013), we reported the results of a statistical analysis of poll data from the Pew Research Center in the lead-up to the 2008 U.S. presidential election. Ghitza and Gelman performed several analyses; in the present article we replicate one of them, an estimate of John McCain’s share of the two-party by income, ethnicity, and state, as summarized in Figure 2 of that earlier article, which displays raw data and estimated McCain support as a function of five income categories for white voters and all voters in each of the 50 states.
targets.outcome_quote: Our replication analysis produced graphs that showed the same general pattern of income and voting as we had found in our earlier published work, but with some differences in particular states that we cannot easily explain and which seem too large to be explained by sampling variation.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors report agreement in broad income-voting patterns and unexplained systematic state-level discrepancies. Calling the preregistered replication worked describes executing the analysis, not a blanket confirmation. The paper combines a same-data Bayesian reanalysis with three different survey samples; coded as replication because the new-sample comparisons are the main completed test. The original-data reanalysis closely recovers predictions and removal of weights leaves jagged patterns, but new-sample discrepancies are not reproduction robustness checks.
